# What Makes the Harness Lab Different — V5.2 operational update

Copyright 2026 Mars Harness Lab contributors. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0.

The work carries forward, and the evidence comes with it. The lab combines specialized science, engineering, and project-management procedures with bounded agents, shared records, independent checks, and human authority.

## Included methods

1. Bounded Tree of Thoughts, competing hypotheses, and design trade studies.
2. Graph-linked wiki memory, provenance, focused retrieval, and downstream change-impact analysis.
3. Approved table-of-contents planning, section contracts, chapter drafting, and common-fact reconciliation.
4. Paired schematics/pinouts/parts/PCB deliverables and synchronized mechanical models/drawings/assembly packages.
5. Experiments, actual simulation execution, verification/validation, calibration, uncertainty, twin readiness, and next-experiment selection.
6. Independent virtual challenge, evidence-backed peer critique, repeated revision/retest, and preserved dissent.
7. Explicit handoffs, bounded parallel work, controlled research returns, and authenticated-adapter requirements.
8. Risk-based action rules, resource budgets, security boundaries, run manifests, hash verification, replay, and regression procedures.
9. Ten additional specialist role contracts, each with inputs, operating instructions, output requirements, ethics, and stops.
10. Comparable measurement of cycle time, human effort, review, rework, cost, and quality.

## Where to find them

The standalone Operational Methods ZIP contains the full pack. Every current individual skill and agent ZIP includes it. Complete skill/agent suites store it under `skills/operational-methods/`; the three-domain setup ZIP stores it under `operational-methods/`. The presentation package's updated `Portable_Skills/operational-methods/` contains the same material. Existing download URLs remain valid.

Read `README.md`, select the method and role, fill the relevant template with approved project data, run the applicable local check, then execute the real task with authorized tools. Use `CAPABILITY_COVERAGE.json` to distinguish available procedures/helpers from external integration requirements.

## What this release does not claim

The included Python utilities check supplied local records. They do not generate an LLM search tree, create a production GraphRAG service, authenticate approvals, enforce system permissions, run CAD/EDA or simulation tools, connect live telemetry, or deploy the three SaaS applications. Those integrations still need implementation and end-to-end validation. The synthetic tests do not qualify a physical design or establish quantified R&D savings.

The existing presentation slides, PDFs, and artwork are unchanged. This addendum and the updated operating packages provide the expanded capabilities without relabeling historical presentation results.
